common_name: Dwarf Emerald Giant Tomato (Green Beefsteak Dwarf Tomato)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost; the sturdy, dwarf-indeterminate plant grows only 2-4 feet tall, making it well suited to large containers and raised beds.

directions: Dwarf Emerald Giant produces large beefsteak-type fruit that ripens from deep green to a green-gold color with an amber blush at the blossom end, revealing translucent lime-green flesh with a rich, spicy-sweet flavor reminiscent of full-size green heirloom beefsteaks. The compact, dwarf-indeterminate plant packs that big-fruit heirloom character onto a manageable 2-4 foot frame suited to raised beds and large containers. It is a release of the Dwarf Tomato Project, the volunteer breeding collaboration begun in 2005 by Craig LeHoullier and Patrina Nuske Small to combine heirloom flavor and color diversity with compact plant habit.

common_name: Dwarf Hannah's Prize Tomato (Orange-Gold Dwarf Beefsteak)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost; the compact, dwarf-indeterminate habit of 2-4 feet suits container growing and small raised beds.

directions: Dwarf Hannah's Prize bears medium-to-large orange-gold beefsteak fruit with the mild, fruity sweetness and creamy texture typical of gold-fruited heirloom tomatoes. Named for a member of the LeHoullier family, it grows as a sturdy, dwarf-indeterminate plant reaching just 2-4 feet, concentrating heirloom-quality fruit onto a footprint well suited to containers and small gardens. It is one of the many named releases from the Dwarf Tomato Project, the volunteer-driven breeding collaboration coordinated by Craig LeHoullier and Patrina Nuske Small since 2005.

common_name: Dwarf Jade Beauty Tomato (Green-When-Ripe Dwarf Tomato)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost; the dense, dwarf-indeterminate 2-4 foot habit makes it a good candidate for large pots and small raised beds.

directions: Dwarf Jade Beauty produces medium round fruit that ripens to a translucent jade-green with an amber blush at the blossom end, offering the sweet-tart, slightly spicy complexity typical of green-when-ripe tomatoes. The plant keeps a compact, dwarf-indeterminate habit of 2-4 feet, making it a practical choice for gardeners with limited space who still want an unusual green-fleshed heirloom. It emerged from the Dwarf Tomato Project, the international volunteer breeding effort founded by Craig LeHoullier and Patrina Nuske Small in 2005 to pair dwarf growth habit with heirloom flavor and color diversity.

common_name: Dwarf Sarah's Delight Tomato (Apricot-Orange Dwarf Tomato)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost; the sturdy, dwarf-indeterminate bush stays 2-4 feet tall, well suited to containers and small gardens.

directions: Dwarf Sarah's Delight bears small-to-medium round fruit in a warm apricot-orange hue with a sweet, mild flavor good for fresh eating and salads. The plant grows as a sturdy, dwarf-indeterminate bush 2-4 feet tall, concentrating heirloom-quality fruit onto a footprint well suited to containers and small raised beds. It was released through the Dwarf Tomato Project, the breeding collaboration founded by Craig LeHoullier and Patrina Nuske Small to pair dwarf growth habit with heirloom flavor and color diversity.

common_name: Dwarf Liz Birt Tomato (Pink Dwarf Beefsteak)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost; the compact, dwarf-indeterminate habit of 2-4 feet suits raised beds and large containers.

directions: Dwarf Liz Birt produces medium-to-large pink beefsteak fruit with the balanced sweet-tart flavor and meaty texture prized in pink heirloom tomatoes. Named in honor of a longtime Dwarf Tomato Project volunteer, the plant keeps a compact, dwarf-indeterminate habit of 2-4 feet that suits raised beds and large containers. It is one of dozens of named cultivars to come out of the Dwarf Tomato Project since its founding in 2005 by Craig LeHoullier and Patrina Nuske Small.

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost; the compact, dwarf-indeterminate plant stays 2-4 feet tall, a good choice for patio containers and small-space gardens.

directions: Dwarf Moonglow bears medium round fruit in a glowing golden-orange color with a mild, sweet flavor and low acidity typical of orange-fruited tomatoes. It grows as a compact, dwarf-indeterminate plant reaching 2-4 feet, making it a good choice for patio containers and small-space vegetable gardens.
